description: REQ-R1 invokes <slot>-cli.sh --restart whenever recipe.action == 'restart'. But health_check_v2.select_fix_recipe maps BOTH issue kinds 'tmux_dead' AND 'stale' to {action: 'restart'} (skills/_shared/lib/health_check_v2.py:97-98). 'stale' fires whenever (now_ts - last_pass_mtime) >= _STALE_SECONDS even though the tmux core is ALIVE. Under live #27 (gig migration is now live, hot path is healthy tmux + noop), this means the very first time the dispatcher sees a stale snapshot it will subprocess.run gig-cli.sh --restart, which executes 'tmux kill-session -t gig-core' (gig-cli.sh:27) on the running INNER worker. This DIRECTLY violates parent INV-P1 ('proactive-loop NEVER stops LAYER C <slot>-cli.sh tmux sessions during normal operation') and the §8 Open-Question resolution ('proactive-loop ever invoke <slot>-cli.sh to restart? YES via STEP 3 dispatch_highest_priority({tmux_dead: true})' — note: tmux_dead ONLY, not stale). Spec must either (a) gate restart on recipe.params or issue.kind == 'tmux_dead' explicitly, or (b) split 'stale' into a non-restart recipe. As written REQ-R1 + the existing recipe map is an INV-P1 violation on the hot path.

evidence.snippet: REQ-R1: WHEN STEP 3 computes recipe.action == 'restart', THE DISPATCHER SHALL invoke the per-slot restart command. For slot 'gig' that command is `bash <ANICCA_HOME>/skills/earn/gig/gig-cli.sh --restart`

secondaryEvidence.snippet: INV-P1: proactive-loop NEVER stops LAYER C <slot>-cli.sh tmux sessions during normal operation
